customer_question: We're getting COM port errors (COM4 Open ERROR, access denied) trying to connect our external PC to the DUT for DTM-mode testing through InterLab's Automation Explore -- what's wrong with our setup, and what should the working configuration look like?
question_variants: Why can't our external PC recognize the virtual COM port for the tester connection?
Do we need a USB-Serial converter cable connected to the external PC's USB port specifically?
What COM port and baud rate settings should Automation Explore use to confirm RF PHY commands are working?
How do we know our DTM-mode connection through InterLab is actually working?
actual_issue: An external PC intended to drive DTM-mode commands to a DUT via InterLab's Automation Explore tool was failing to recognize the relevant virtual COM port, producing COM4 Open ERROR and access-denied errors, and it needed to be determined whether this was a cabling/configuration problem and what the correct end-to-end setup should be.
plain_english_explanation: To control a test device in a special radio test mode from an external PC through the lab's automation tool, several physical cable connections have to be in place -- a USB-to-serial converter cable on the PC side, and a cross cable on the device side. If any of these aren't actually plugged in, the PC simply can't see the virtual COM port it needs, which produces exactly the kind of connection errors seen here. Once everything is properly connected, the lab's tool can be configured with the right port and speed settings to confirm communication is working.
consultant_answer: The DUT itself should be connected on COM3. For the external PC's connection to be recognized, the USB-Serial converter cable's RS232C side must actually be connected to the external PC -- without that physical connection, the external PC cannot recognize the virtual COM port at all, which explains why COM4 Open ERROR and COM4 access-denied errors were occurring: the USB-Serial converter cable was not yet connected to the external PC's USB port (the team had a cross cable still pending, which was a separate, expected gap). Once the cross cable is obtained and the RF test is complete, connect everything and retry. Once the DTM-mode-entry app was confirmed working, the next step was to use InterLab's Automation Explore to configure the external PC's USB-Serial converter cable COM# setting at 9600bps, first selecting the HCI-Serial interface, and to verify success by checking whether the RF PHY command confirmation displays green.
decision_logic: COM-port recognition failures on an external PC connecting to a DUT through a lab automation tool should first be checked against the physical cabling chain (USB-Serial converter cable to the PC's USB port, cross cable to the DUT side) before suspecting a software or DUT problem, since a missing cable connection alone fully explains COM-open and access-denied errors; once cabling is complete, the correct verification is the automation tool's COM port/baud-rate/interface configuration confirming a green (success) indicator on RF PHY command communication.
final_recommendation: Verify the full physical cabling chain (USB-Serial converter cable into the external PC's USB port, cross cable to the DUT side) before treating COM port errors as a software issue. Once cabling is complete and the DTM-mode app is confirmed working, configure InterLab's Automation Explore with the correct COM port and 9600bps baud rate, select the HCI-Serial interface, and confirm the RF PHY command check shows green before proceeding with testing.
risk_if_done_wrong: Treating COM port open/access-denied errors as a DUT or software fault instead of a missing cable connection wastes troubleshooting time and delays reaching the actual RF PHY test setup verification step.
